packageRules.description: A patch or minor update that passes CI - lint, types, tests and a build - lands on its own. A major does not: it is read first.
unicoen.ts is frozen upstream: PLIVET's C interpreter is a subclass of it, and what a release would change is the parser everything else is built on. It moves by hand or not at all.
Build tooling. Webpack, Babel and the loaders move together or not at all - a loader ahead of the webpack it plugs into is the usual way this breaks.
Tests. Jest and ts-jest are a compatible set - the suite stops running when they are not - so they are updated as one.
Lint and format. typescript-eslint tracks both ESLint and TypeScript, so a lone bump of either is the one that fails.
The editor. The @codemirror packages share one document model and are versioned against each other.
What the interpreter and the browser build need underneath them: the Node builtins webpack 5 no longer polyfills on its own, and the two small libraries the core uses.
The Node baseline is what CI pins and what `engines` states; moving it is a decision, not an update.
